data.description:
## Incident Overview

Outbound comment sync re-emits the same update on every reconciler pass because add_comment fails and the failure is swallowed.

## Observed (live evidence)
- reconcile-bridge run 27033213227 (2026-06-05, sha 46e1858fdb / current main), key DIG-4292:
  `update_one: add_comment failed for DIG-4292: AcliMutationError('ACLI mutation reported FAILURE (exit=0) for [acli, jira, workitem, comment, create, --key, DIG-4292, --body, PREPLANNING_CONTEXT: {large JSON...}]')`
- The batch_outcome is recorded `action=update key=DIG-4292 error=None` (the comment sub-failure does NOT surface in the outcome).
- Because the comment never lands in Jira, the outbound differ sees it as still-missing and re-emits the update EVERY pass. Pass 1 applied 897 mutations; pass 2 still applied 16 (these non-404 keys: DIG-4292/4933/5294/5347/5383/5522/5528 among them) -> never converges to 0.

## Expected
After a successful pass, a synced comment must be considered converged so the differ stops re-emitting. The outbound comment sync must not loop forever on a body ACLI/Jira rejects.

## Constraint on fix (user directive)
Truncating an over-length comment for the Jira side is ACCEPTABLE if the root cause is a Jira/ACLI comment field-length/size limit -- BUT the truncated form must NOT be written back to the local ticket (no round-trip corruption of local content), and the differ must treat the synced (possibly truncated) state as converged.

## Related
- INC-010 (status-fallback comment) is a DIFFERENT comment path; not this bug.
- 1e08 (bound-but-absent re-emitter) is the OTHER convergence cause (deleted/Done-out-of-window keys); separate root cause.

## Root cause (to verify experimentally)
Why does ACLI comment create return FAILURE(exit=0) on these bodies? Candidates: Jira comment size limit (~32767 chars / 32KB ADF), special content (PREPLANNING_CONTEXT JSON), or ADF encoding.
data.title: [reconciler/applier]: add_comment FAILURE(exit=0) on large comment body -> never lands, perpetual outbound re-emit
